hints: Take natural logarithms of $P = a\mathrm{e}^{kt}$ to form $\ln P = kt + \ln a$.
Match gradient $m = k = \dfrac{1}{20}$ and intercept $C = \ln a = 3$ to solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Take natural logarithms of both sides of $P = a\mathrm{e}^{kt}$:
$$\ln P = \ln(a\mathrm{e}^{kt}) = \ln a + \ln(\mathrm{e}^{kt}) = kt + \ln a$$

Compare with the standard linear form $Y = mX + C$ where $Y = \ln P$ and $X = t$:
$$\text{Gradient } m = k$$
$$\text{Vertical intercept } C = \ln a$$

State the value of $k$ from the given gradient:
$$k = \dfrac{1}{20} = 0.05$$

Use the given vertical intercept $(0, 3)$ to find $a$:
$$\ln a = 3 \implies a = \mathrm{e}^3 \approx 20.0855 \dots$$

Round $a$ correct to 2 significant figures:
$$a = 20$$
State the parameters: $k = \dfrac{1}{20}, \quad a = 20$.

ai_rubric.Linearising Mathematical Models: States or implies $\ln P = \ln a + kt$ (B1). States $k = 1/20$ (B1). Finds $a = e^3 \approx 20$ to 2 s.f. from $\ln a = 3$ (B1).

hints: Set $P = 2a$ in the model equation: $2a = a\mathrm{e}^{kt} \implies 2 = \mathrm{e}^{kt}$.
Solve $kt = \ln 2$ using $k = \dfrac{1}{20}$, and round the doubling time to the nearest hour.
walkthrough:
Set the population to double its initial value $a$:
$$P = 2a$$
$$a\mathrm{e}^{kt} = 2a \implies \mathrm{e}^{kt} = 2$$

Take the natural logarithm of both sides:
$$kt = \ln 2$$
$$t = \dfrac{\ln 2}{k}$$

Round to the nearest whole hour:
$$t = 14 \text{ hours}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Forms equation $e^{kt} = 2$ or $kt = \ln 2$ (M1). Obtains $t = 14$ hours to the nearest hour (A1).
